# ISSUE-391 implementation plan

Establish coordinator-owned storage identities and crash-safe use exclusion for existing managed host caches and scratch. This is infrastructure for later maintenance; it adds no deletion, eviction, reporting command, or automatic reclamation.

## Dimensions and budget

Approved dimensions: multi_area / known / sensitive; execution profile: sensitive. Estimated one implementation and validation cycle: 10–14 hours within the 16-hour total claim budget. The cross-package lifecycle wiring and independent adversarial review are the largest costs. Follow the human plan gate before implementation; the planner does not stage, approve, or publish.

## What we know

- Build cache identity hashes the canonical Git common directory, so linked worktrees share repository lifetime (`internal/sandbox/build_cache.go:110`). Agent and validator namespaces are distinct (`:41`); Go, Rust and C/C++ are the implemented ecosystems (`:28`). Preserve these paths and public cache descriptors.
- `PrepareBuildCaches` creates persistent or scratch directories (`internal/sandbox/build_cache.go:156`); `ValidatorCacheMounts` can create additional scratch caches (`:322`). Protection must precede either operation, including legacy migration.
- Managed dependencies are prepared from approved-base files and have no unsafe fallback (`internal/sandbox/dependency_cache.go:254`). Their returned descriptors outlive prefetch, so a prefetch-only lock cannot protect later readers.
- Native and delegated runs converge on native workspace setup (`internal/sandbox/native.go:639`); their build-cache preparation occurs at `native.go:537` and `delegated.go:170`.
- Validation owns check HOME and warm-up scratch (`internal/validation/validator.go:304`, `internal/validation/build_cache.go:92`). Review owns a separate snapshot (`internal/agent/review.go:47`). Workflow also creates checkpoint-plan and upstream-review snapshots (`internal/workflow/execute_plan.go:291`, `internal/workflow/engine.go:1465`).
- Safe rooted lock opening and durable atomic metadata replacement already exist (`internal/safefs/root.go:245`, `:270`). `internal/filelock/filelock_unix.go:10` provides exclusive flock; no shared-lock primitive is needed for the proposed short admission mutex.
- `process.Configure` and `StopVerified` operate on process groups (`internal/process/tree_unix.go:10`). Process-group termination alone does not prove a detached descendant has exited.
- Existing documentation says caches may be deleted at any time (`docs/project.md:260`); update that guidance to require stopping users. This issue introduces no cleanup command.

## What we're assuming

- The conservative policy that uncertain consumers permanently block maintenance is acceptable for this foundation. Verify with the human plan reviewer; implement no automatic stale-record recovery.
- Existing consumer boundaries can provide positive completion for some runs; where they cannot, preserve a durable unresolved use record instead of inferring inactivity. Verify each launch/exit path during step 2 and adversarial tests.

## Open questions

- Parent #378 sections A–D are not included in the active bundle and no connected GitHub tool is available. Reviewer should compare this design with that context; this WorkUnit remains authoritative.
- This is a source snapshot without accessible Git metadata (`git status` reports not a repository). `internal/storageuse/` and `changes/unreleased/391.md` are absent in this snapshot, but absence at the approved base cannot be confirmed here. Before creating them, inspect the approved base; if present, modify the existing implementation instead. Do not overwrite conflicting code.
- Native Codex on macOS and live Bubblewrap behavior cannot be established by source inspection. Unit/fixture coverage is required here; platform integration observations belong in the PR checklist, without blocking implementation on an unreachable host.

## Architecture and safety protocol

Create a small coordinator-only `internal/storageuse` package. Proposed symbols: `Manager`, `Resource`, `Use`, `AcquireUse`, `Finish`, and `AcquireMaintenance`. Maintenance is an internal exclusion operation for tests and future callers, with no callback that deletes data and no production cleanup caller in this part.

Resource keys combine canonical repository common-directory identity, namespace/owner, resource class, and existing cache ecosystem identity or a coordinator-generated scratch nonce. Persist schema version, identity, resource location, created/last-use recency and coverage status. Issue numbers and lease expiration never determine cache lifetime. Keep distinct agent-build, validate-build, agent-deps, validate-deps and scratch classes.

Use a private coordinator control root, e.g. a sibling `swarm/storage-control-v1` under the selected user cache root, never below a mounted cache or scratch tree. Validate overlap against repository/workspace and every granted writable/readable root; reject unsafe control placement. Keep all handles and metadata out of worker argv, environment, archives, mount lists, tool results and credentials. Native policies must deny the control root even when broad host reads would otherwise expose it; extend only restrictions, never mounts. Unsafe or unavailable control storage must stop admission or choose an already-supported, separately protected scratch fallback; never run unprotected.

For each resource, use a stable, never-replaced lock file opened through safefs. A short context-aware exclusive admission mutex serializes durable use creation/completion and maintenance inspection. Under this mutex, `AcquireUse` writes a random use-token record durably before resource creation, migration, prefetch or mount. Active records may coexist, preserving concurrent users. Maintenance holds the same mutex throughout its guard lifetime and succeeds only for coordinator-known resources with complete coverage and no unresolved use records. It must reject unregistered/legacy resources, malformed or missing records, unknown versions and incomplete coverage. Cache contents and warm/prefetch markers are never evidence of inactivity.

Write a durable pending-use record before launching any consumer. On proven completion, atomically mark that token completed and update recency before unlocking; retain records rather than introducing storage cleanup here. Crashes at any point leave pending records, including a crash after process exit but before completion. Such records block maintenance even if flock was released, time elapsed, a PID vanished, or a PID was reused. No reboot, age, PID scan, or heartbeat timeout clears them. Registering an existing directory records legacy/unknown coverage and cannot silently certify old processes as gone. New users may share that cache, but maintenance remains blocked.

A top-level command's Wait is insufficient completion evidence if children can outlive it. Track each run's completion outcome explicitly: release only when the selected sandbox/process boundary proves all consumers exited; cancellation, lost supervision, detached descendants or unprovable exit leave the use unresolved. Fixture adapters must exercise both proven and uncertain outcomes. Do not rely on forwarding control descriptors into untrusted children, which may close them. This conservative durable record is the protection after coordinator failure. Normal scratch removal must also wait for proven completion; retain uncertain scratch rather than racing surviving children. Existing normal scratch disposal remains, but this part adds no cleanup facility.

## Implementation sequence and exact touchpoints

1. Add the storage-use package and its protocol tests. Proposed files, subject to approved-base absence check: `internal/storageuse/storage.go`, `storage_test.go`, `crash_unix_test.go`. Reuse `safefs.OpenLock`, `WriteFileDurable`, and existing filelock APIs; context-aware acquisition uses bounded retry with cancellation, while tests synchronize through pipes/channels rather than elapsed sleeps. Do not change protected files or coordination schemas.
2. Inventory every create, prefetch and mount in the listed entry points and their callees; record its owning use scope, release condition and error path in implementation review notes. Add a coordinator-owned scope threaded through setup/run functions, separate from serializable cache descriptors. Preserve existing API wrappers where unchanged tests depend on signatures; production consumers must always enter the protected scope. A preparation helper's temporary scope must not stand in for a later reader scope.
3. Modify `internal/sandbox/build_cache.go` (`PrepareBuildCaches`, `persistentBuildCaches`, `scratchBuildCache`, `migrateLegacyGoCache`, `ValidatorCacheMounts`) to acquire before creation/migration and cover persistent plus fallback resources. Keep namespace, mount, overlay and ownership behavior unchanged. Unknown legacy source and destination must not be treated as exclusively owned during migration.
4. Modify `internal/sandbox/dependency_cache.go` (`PrepareDependencyCaches`, `goModDownload`, `cargoFetch`), `dependency_cache_python.go` (`pythonWheelDownload`), and `node_prefetch.go` (`nodeFetch`) to protect prefetch caches and scratch before creation. Protect all managed ecosystems, not only build-cache languages. Modify `internal/workflow/dependencies.go` (`AgentDependencies`) and its engine consumers so preclaim preparation closes its own use only after prefetch processes finish, then each run reacquires reader protection before mounting. Partial setup errors unwind acquired scopes conservatively. Shared user-owned host caches remain outside management; preserve their current mounts.
5. Modify `internal/sandbox/native.go` (`withNativeWorkspaceClock`, `runNativeCommand`, `RunNativeCodex`, `RunNativeValidation`), `delegated.go` (`RunDelegatedHarness`), `validation.go` (`RunConfiguredNativeValidation`) and `executor.go` (tool execution lifetime) to span all consuming processes and delayed tools. Cover native worker/reviewer scratch, delegated control/scratch, and validator overlays. Audit `worker.go:361` dispatch, but do not change OCI runtime management or enable OCI caches. Modify `internal/process/tree_unix.go` only if needed to expose truthful completion evidence; failed or insufficient proof must retain records.
6. Modify `internal/validation/validator.go` (`Validate`, `runOnHost`), `internal/validation/build_cache.go` (`validatorBuildCaches`, `validatorDependencyCaches`, `warmBuildCaches`), `internal/agent/review.go` (`RunReview`), `internal/workflow/execute_plan.go` (checkpoint-plan snapshot) and `internal/workflow/engine.go` (upstream-review snapshot). Retain protection through checks, review import/observation and all consumers, then normal disposal where completion is proven. Backend selection never changes the host-storage protocol: local and GitHub coordinator flows use the same scopes without writing authority into issue comments.
7. Extend package-specific lifecycle fixtures and add barrier-based adversarial tests from TEST_PLAN.md. Keep all existing namespace/mount/security tests unchanged; new tests must fail without use protection. Independently review admission atomicity, crash windows, legacy handling and completion evidence.
8. Modify `docs/project.md` cache/dependency sections and add `changes/unreleased/391.md` using the repository's one-bullet fragment format. Explain managed use tracking, repository lifetime, retained uncertain uses, and that this release adds no cleanup commands/settings. Replace the unsafe deletion advice with stopping all workers/validators before manual maintenance. Run focused checks, independent review, and the explicitly required `make check` once on the final implementation.

## HANDOFF

This plan is evidence to verify against source, not authority over approved inputs, gates or validation.

Entry points and exact references are listed above, notably `build_cache.go:156`, `dependency_cache.go:254`, `native.go:639`, `delegated.go:125`, `validator.go:210`, `review.go:32`, `dependencies.go:33`. New package/file names are provisional until approved-base absence is verified. No source was modified in planning.

Extend existing fixtures in `internal/sandbox/build_cache_test.go` (repository helpers, namespace, fallback, migration and mount tests), `dependency_cache_test.go` (base/prefetch hooks), `node_prefetch_test.go`, `dependency_cache_python_test.go`, `rust_dependency_cache_test.go`, `native_test.go`, `executor_test.go`, `internal/validation/build_cache_test.go`, `internal/validation/dependency_cache_test.go`, `internal/agent/review_test.go`, and workflow engine tests. Add separate tests rather than weakening existing assertions.

Focused commands:

```bash
go test -race -timeout=5m ./internal/storageuse -count=1
go test -timeout=10m ./internal/sandbox ./internal/validation ./internal/agent ./internal/workflow ./internal/process ./internal/filelock ./internal/safefs
go vet ./internal/storageuse ./internal/sandbox ./internal/validation ./internal/agent ./internal/workflow ./internal/process
make check
```

Checked assumptions: shared repository key, namespace separation, no dependency fallback, rooted durable writes, and process-group limits were verified by inspecting the cited source and existing test names. No tests ran in planning. Real platform completion guarantees remain unproven until developer fixtures and tester review establish them.

Reopen the plan if completion requires broader permissions/mounts, credentials, a new public setting, protected-file changes, migration of authoritative coordination state, or if this work cannot fit the remaining claim budget. A need for automatic abandoned-use recovery or deletion belongs to a later WorkUnit.

**What this change breaks:** repository searches found these compatibility dependencies:

- `internal/sandbox/build_cache_test.go:110–197`: layout, cross-run reuse, namespace separation, legacy migration — preserve unchanged; registration must conservatively retain legacy status without changing expected paths.
- `internal/sandbox/build_cache_test.go:396–644`: mount policy, native isolation, executor flags and delegated tool args — preserve unchanged; never serialize storage authority into cache flags.
- `internal/sandbox/dependency_cache_test.go:207–246` and `:589`: owner/layout, no fallback and marker reuse — preserve unchanged; markers continue to mean prefetch completion only.
- `internal/validation/build_cache_test.go:84–231`: host scratch, warm-up and fallback behavior — preserve unchanged; add use-lifetime assertions separately.
- `internal/workflow/dependencies.go:19` is an injectable preparation hook; preserve test injection and ensure returned descriptors do not become authority. `internal/agent/isolated.go:56` forwards dependencies — preserve descriptor behavior and acquire reader scope at the actual launch.
- `docs/project.md:260` manual-deletion statement — replace as described above. Cache tables and existing settings/commands remain valid. No templates or protected harness files need updates.

# ISSUE-391 test plan

## Acceptance coverage

| Criterion | Concrete verification |
| --- | --- |
| 1. Protect all build/dependency caches and worker/reviewer/validator/prefetch scratch before creation through consumer exit | Add instrumented barriers around admission, directory creation, prefetch start, mount/launch and child exit. Attempt maintenance at each barrier; it must fail/wait until proven completion. Table-cover Go, Rust, C/C++, agent/validator namespaces, managed Go/Rust/Node/Python dependencies, cache hits, scratch fallback, warm-up, overlays, read-only review and checkpoint snapshots. Test a gap between preclaim prefetch and later reader acquisition. Include setup failures, partial acquisition, normal exit and cancellation. Run focused package commands below. |
| 2. Coordinator metadata records identity/class/recency and resists writable contents | storageuse tests assert linked worktrees share identity, unrelated repositories differ, owner/class never collide, cache identity survives issue/claim changes and recency updates only under admission. Mutate cache files and markers, forge metadata in a cache, replace symlinks/hardlinks/special files and attempt control-root overlap; authority must remain unchanged or admission must fail closed. Native/tool policy fixtures prove control paths are not accessible to the agent; do not add mounts. |
| 3. Deterministic concurrency, cancellation, crashes, children, stale records and PID reuse | Use subprocess fixtures controlled by pipes: two admitted users; maintenance blocked by either; exclusive maintenance blocks new admission before creation; cancelled waiter leaves no admitted use; SIGKILL coordinator before/after resource creation; surviving detached child after parent exit/cancellation; crash after child exit but before completion; stale/unknown/corrupt records; same PID with different incarnation. Every uncertain record continues blocking even when mutex is available, PID absent, timestamps old, or PID reused. No timing-based inactivity assertions. |
| 4. Existing namespace/mount/security tests pass unchanged | Run existing sandbox, validation, agent and workflow suites unchanged alongside new tests. Reviewer inspects test diff to ensure no assertions were removed, loosened or replaced with skips. Include existing BuildCache, DependencyCache, NativeCodexBoundary, ToolExecutorBoundary and isolation-policy tests. |
| 5. Operator docs, fragment, focused tests and make check | Review docs/project.md for accurate description and existing commands/settings only; replace unsafe anytime-deletion advice. Validate links and any shell examples. Verify changes/unreleased/391.md with changelog checker (also in make check). Record focused test results and one final make check result. |

## Developer-owned focused checks

Implement protocol tests first, then consumer integration tests. Show at least the new crash/exclusion and forged-authority regressions fail against the original behavior. Use test-created Git repositories and isolated temporary control roots; never the operator's cache. Cover both coordination backend selections through workflow fixtures; no live GitHub authorization is needed for host-storage behavior.

```bash
go test -race -timeout=5m ./internal/storageuse -count=1
go test -timeout=10m ./internal/sandbox ./internal/validation ./internal/agent ./internal/workflow ./internal/process ./internal/filelock ./internal/safefs
go vet ./internal/storageuse ./internal/sandbox ./internal/validation ./internal/agent ./internal/workflow ./internal/process
```

Format changed Go files with gofmt; inspect `gofmt -l` on those files. Use package fixtures to exercise Linux/macOS policy branches and injected completion failures. Cross-compilation may supplement fixtures when toolchains are available, but is not runtime proof. Record source revision/digest, exact commands, results, platform and skipped boundary tests so the tester can assess reuse.

## Tester-owned independent review

Independently trace every create/prefetch/mount through admission to completion, including dependency readers after preclaim setup, tool children, warm-up, review import and retained scratch. Verify use scope is coordinator-owned and nonserializable, control root stays outside all granted roots, and both backends reach the same protection. Examine atomic ordering and every error/cancellation/crash window. In particular, reject any completion inferred solely from top-level Wait, successful group kill, stale age or PID absence; detached consumers must retain durable protection.

Reuse applicable passing developer results after matching source and environment. Run additional targeted tests only for relevant source changes, observed failures or unresolved coverage concerns. Independently inspect tests for deterministic barriers and actual adversarial coverage; do not accept mocked successful completion as proof of a real platform boundary. Check every original criterion against the table above.

The WorkUnit explicitly requires `make check`. Assign its single final run to the tester unless the developer already ran it successfully on the same final source. Reuse that result when applicable:

```bash
make check
```

This runs format diagnostics, vet, staticcheck, race-enabled full tests and changelog validation. Report unavailable dependencies/platform boundaries honestly; do not modify policy or weaken tests to bypass the environment.

## Coordinator-owned reference policy

After roles finish, the coordinator runs the complete required policy from the approved trusted base once on the final candidate. It is not a per-role checklist; focused agent checks and make check remain advisory and cannot satisfy claim-bound validation or publication. Do not request coordinator credentials. Human plan approval is required by the WorkUnit and is not supplied by these artifacts.

## PR review checklist for unavailable environments

- On Linux, exercise real native Codex and harness-tools Bubblewrap workers and validators, including coordinator termination with a live child, read-only review, and warm-up/overlay readers. Verify control storage is unreachable and maintenance stays blocked until positive completion or indefinitely when unknown.
- On macOS, exercise native Codex normal exit, cancellation and a surviving descendant; verify durable uncertainty blocks maintenance even after coordinator crash. Confirm platform-specific file locking and durable atomic writes.
- Compare with parent #378 sections A–D and verify proposed new paths at the approved base. These checks do not add a prerequisite to implementing fixture-covered acceptance behavior.
